== Biography ==
Elizabeth was baptised. She is the daughter of [[Glasgow-3324|William Glasgow]] and [[Stewart-72380|Elizabeth Stewart]].

* 15. William3 Glasgow, b. 1763, 6. 1816, m. Elizabeth, had daughters Jane, Eliza and Mary. Buried St. Cedma's Cemetery in Larne. This could be the William Glasgow, captain of the "William," advertised in the Belfast News Letter 1792-1799.
* 1802 – August 30, 1802 – Elizabeth Glasgow was baptised, daughter of William Glasgow and Elizabeth Stewart, Corran. (Corran being the peninsula in Larne where the Olderfleet Castle ruins stand).<ref>www.wikitree.com/wiki/Space%3AChronology_of_the_Glasgow_Family_in_Northern_Ireland_in_Historical_Context</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-3324]] is assessed at 94% (proved). The Larne monument transcription in Ulster Journal of Archaeology6(1900), p.47 identifies Eliza in William and Elizabeth Glasgow’s family, alongside William’s 1816 death. The 1802 Stewart baptism is a compatible additional identity lead, requiring an original check.

Selected father-profile identity and paternal relationship; maternal identity is separate.

Next useful test: Compare the original stone and William’s 1815 will, PRONI D300/1/5/49.

Source basis already held: [https://archive.org/details/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/page/47/mode/1up "Armorial Sculptured Stones of the County Antrim," Ulster Journal of Archaeology, second series, vol. 6 (1900), p. 47, Glasgow inscriptions; page image (https://archive.org/details/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/page/47/mode/1up).]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.
